---
title: "Instructors and Maintainers"
---

Students run `init`, `fetch`, `run`, and `report`. Everything on this page
validates the suite itself or grades what students submit.

## Auditing the Registry Contract

```bash
mlperf audit                  # label and metadata contract for all workloads
mlperf audit --policy public  # the stricter public-result contract
```

`audit` inspects registry metadata without running anything. It checks that
score-bearing workloads declare complete quality targets, that datasets and
models carry source and license information, and that public statuses are
internally consistent. Run it after any registry edit.

## Validation Presets

```bash
mlperf validate smoke                 # fast end-to-end sanity, dry-run friendly
mlperf validate coverage              # every suite exercised
mlperf validate max                   # the full comparable profile
mlperf validate release --output-dir submissions/validation
```

Presets execute workloads and grade the artifacts they produce. `smoke` is
suitable for CI; `release` is the bar a public release must clear and can run
with `--keep-going --skip-doctor` for long unattended passes.

## Grading Student Submissions

```bash
mlperf grade submissions --output submissions/grade.json
```

`grade` walks a directory of submissions, verifies each `.provd` manifest,
re-checks quality-target satisfaction, and emits a machine-readable grade
file. Because provenance artifacts carry hashes of the trained state and the
environment fingerprint, grading does not require re-running student code.

## Course Integration Pattern

A benchmark-backed assignment follows one shape. Students run the reference
baseline (`mlperf run --workload X --profile max`), read the report to find
the bottleneck, implement an optimization as a
[SUT plugin](sut-plugins.qmd), and submit the packaged result
(`mlperf package`). The instructor grades the directory in one command. The
lab files under `examples/` are ready-made instances of this pattern.

## Keeping the Docs Honest

Benchmark pages on this site are generated from the registry:

```bash
python3 tools/generate_docs.py           # regenerate after registry edits
python3 tools/generate_docs.py --check   # CI gate: fail on drift
```

If you change a workload YAML and the site, the `--check` gate fails until the
pages are regenerated, so documentation and harness cannot disagree.
